question.title: What will SpaceX's (SPCX) closing share price be on Friday, November 27, 2026?
question.description:
SpaceX (legal name Space Exploration Technologies Corp., ticker SPCX, Nasdaq Global Select Market) completed the largest IPO in history in June 2026: it priced at $135.00 per share on June 11, 2026, sold 555.6 million primary shares to raise roughly $75 billion, and announced on June 15, 2026 that the offering had closed including full exercise of the underwriters' option (https://ir.spacex.com/updates/releases-details/2026/Space-Exploration-Technologies-Corp--Announces-Closing-of-Initial-Public-Offering-Including-Full-Exercise-of-Underwriters-Option-to-Purchase-Additional-Shares-2026-RgoR-Y1Vwh). The stock opened for its first trade at $150 and closed its first day near $161, implying a valuation of roughly $2.1 trillion.

The shares have been volatile since. The 52-week range is about $104.83 to $225.64, and at ~$137 the market capitalization is roughly $1.9 trillion. Recent daily closes (per Yahoo Finance and market news reports): Nov 6 $134.27; Nov 9 $142.07 (+5.81%); Nov 10 $143.09; Nov 11 $139.75 (-2.33%); Nov 12 $139.94; Nov 13 $136.99 (about -2% on the day). Daily volumes have been heavy, in the 60-115 million share range, and single-day moves of 2-6% have been common since listing — typical for a recently listed mega-cap with a very small public float (only around 5% of shares were sold in the IPO).

Factors in play over the next two weeks:
- Starship Flight 15 was scheduled to launch from Starbase, Texas as soon as 22:45 UTC on November 13, 2026 (after the Nov 13 market close), with an attempted first catch of both stages; the outcome was not yet known when this question was written and is a plausible driver of the Nov 16 session.
- The main 180-day lock-up expires on December 8, 2026, releasing roughly 798 million additional shares — just after this question's resolution date, but widely cited as an overhang weighing on the stock in the interim. An application to fast-track S&P 500 inclusion was reportedly denied, partly due to the low public float.
- The stock trades with no dividend, so the "Close" and "Adj Close" values on the historical table coincide.
- The U.S. equity market is closed on Thursday, November 26, 2026 (Thanksgiving) and holds an early close at 1:00 p.m. ET on Friday, November 27, 2026 (https://www.nasdaqtrader.com/trader.aspx?id=calendar). Holiday-shortened sessions often see thinner volume and outsized single-day moves.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the closing price of Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A common stock (ticker SPCX, listed on Nasdaq) for the U.S. regular trading session of Friday, November 27, 2026, as shown in the "Close" column of the SPCX historical data table on Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SPCX/history/. For example, if that page reports a close of $152.40 for November 27, 2026, the question resolves as 152.40.
question.fine_print:
November 27, 2026 is a scheduled shortened session: the regular session closes at 1:00 p.m. ET, and only the official closing price of that regular session counts (not pre-market, after-hours, or any other post-close trading).

If no closing price is reported for the November 27, 2026 session (for example, because the session is cancelled or SPCX never trades that day), the question resolves to the most recent closing price reported for SPCX before that date.

If the Yahoo Finance page is unavailable or does not show a November 27, 2026 row, the closing price for that session as reported by Nasdaq or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
